count_unit: distinct primary-source documents, not independent organizations or unique events

sources.evidence_note: Explains storage-service scaling, event-loop delay and connection-pool feedback; the traffic scale is OpenAI's own operational report.
Introduces a data-analysis agent for connected company information; product availability does not establish accuracy on every enterprise dataset.
Announces a public-beta managed agent service with sessions, tools and sandboxes; beta status and application-specific controls remain relevant.
Packages financial-services workflows and integrations; a vendor launch provides no independent evidence of investment performance or regulatory compliance.
Describes a researcher using agents in antimicrobial discovery; a research workflow case does not demonstrate an approved therapy.
Introduces full-duplex voice access through an API; realtime behavior still depends on application integration and operating conditions.
Documents detected misuse during December 2025–August 2026; the report's publication date is later than the observed activities.
Explains enterprise applications of Astra after its earlier launch; September 9 is the follow-up article date.
Reports a claimed Navier–Stokes result from a stronger internal model and formalization work; independent acceptance was not established here.
Announces updated image-generation capabilities; examples selected by the provider do not establish universal editing fidelity.
Describes an AI-assisted quantum-experiment workflow; observed assistance is distinct from autonomous scientific validation.
Reports a customer engineering-productivity study; its estimates depend on that organization's workflows and measurement choices.
Describes internal research acceleration and usage; activity measures alone cannot establish a causal gain in scientific discovery.
Presents Astra's safety assessment and cyber-risk classification under OpenAI's framework; this is the provider's assessment.
Introduces Astra and describes capability and safeguard evaluations; benchmark outcomes depend on model configuration and deployment controls.
Explains deployment decisions around frontier cyber capabilities; the article documents a company's risk-management approach.
Describes organizational adoption through recurring workflows; examples do not establish a representative economy-wide productivity effect.
Announces connections to healthcare records and industry data; integration availability does not replace clinical review or access governance.
Introduces Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 with different safeguard and access arrangements; deployment tier affects available behavior.
Describes planned enterprise safeguards and customer-controlled storage; announced future features should not be treated as already deployed.
Reports an advertising revenue run rate; an annualized pace is different from recognized revenue over a completed year.
Discusses alignment and security practices, including reduced-safeguard testing; test incidents should not be attributed to every public deployment.
Explains OpenAI's announced response to Cursor's acquisition; a planned service cutoff is a future event and a party's account.
Previews an interface connecting models and physical instruments; research-preview status limits claims about production interoperability.
Expands scientist access through an initial program; offered seats do not prove downstream research outcomes.
Provides a later account of the Hugging Face evaluation incident; reduced-safeguard internal testing differs from ordinary product access.
Describes a vertically integrated compute strategy; strategic intent and announced capacity differ from delivered operating resources.
Reports inference-hardware results; performance claims depend on workload, precision, utilization and comparison conditions.
Adds administrative tools to agent workflows; changes require appropriately scoped organizational permissions.
Describes model integration into Kiro; integration and price-performance positioning do not prove task-specific superiority.
Describes Replit's use of Luna to broaden software creation; provider adoption is separate from independently measured user success.
Previews private safety processing for zero-data-retention access; retention commitments should be read with their stated processing boundaries.
Explains pacing of model development in response to cyber capabilities; this is an organizational policy, not a universal safety guarantee.
Reports a rapid Asana migration with human review; estimated prior effort and limited cost figures cannot establish universal return on investment.
Explains planned probabilistic text watermarking; statistical detection cannot establish authorship with certainty for every passage.
Previews faster inference under specified service conditions; peak speed claims should not be extrapolated to every workload.
Studies enterprise movement toward execution-oriented usage; token-use patterns are not direct measures of labor productivity.
Expands access to defensive cyber models through AWS; availability depends on program eligibility and applicable safeguards.
Describes AI adoption in a finance organization; an executive's experience is a case study with limited generalizability.
Expands a controlled cyber-defense program; model capability and permitted access remain separate questions.
Reports changes to biological safeguards and false-positive testing; test-set improvements do not guarantee the same effect in every deployment.
Describes external cyber evaluations using less restricted model configurations; those settings differ from ordinary public access.
Explains realtime voice-system engineering; responsiveness depends on the complete serving and interaction pipeline.
Reports mathematical and theoretical-computing results; this review did not independently reproduce proofs or establish external acceptance.
Presents a corporate thesis about abundant intelligence and economic expansion; forward-looking expectations are not realized financial results.
Describes improvements in model price-performance; prices and comparative performance refer to the announcement's conditions and date.
Analyzes three incidents during cybersecurity evaluations; the incidents demonstrate specific control failures, not a population-wide failure rate.
Shows benchmark sensitivity to harness settings and retained reasoning; an improved score alone does not isolate better model weights.
Explains joint optimization of models, inference and agent harnesses; end-to-end gains cannot be assigned to one component without ablation.
Announces academic-research access with later enrollment updates; headline program capacity differs from actual admitted participants.
Discusses agent-assisted modernization of scientific software; correctness and numerical validation remain necessary for each application.
Sets out a conditional position on open weights; it is a company's policy argument rather than binding regulation.
Expands Cognizant's enterprise partnership and Claude deployment; commercial adoption claims are issued by the participating provider.
Introduces Opus 5; comparisons should preserve the tested model, harness, task distribution and access conditions.
Introduces task-scoped production agents with escalation; operational autonomy still requires clear authority and human handling of exceptions.
Describes a planned Georgia data-center buildout; proposed future power capacity is not current operational capacity.
Adds conversational access to Economic Index data; platform usage is a selected sample of activity rather than the entire labor market.
Provides an initial security-incident notice; the later account in S026 supplies additional context and should be consulted.
Describes alignment issues in long-horizon model testing; longer sessions require monitoring and cannot establish guaranteed obedience.
Describes automated adversarial training and red teaming; performance against tested attacks does not establish immunity to unseen attacks.
Discusses evaluating agent investments through useful work and cost; this is an operating framework rather than audited realized returns.
Introduces the GPT-5.6 family; subsequent launches and price updates supersede parts of this historical announcement.
Describes UST's use of Claude in physical-AI applications; integration plans require separate real-world reliability and safety validation.
Audits coding-evaluation problems and measurement noise; flaws reported in one benchmark do not invalidate all software evaluation.
Explains Fable's cyber safeguards and jailbreak process; the scope of permitted access matters when interpreting capability results.
Announces Fable's redeployment after a restriction; this later update changes how the earlier suspension should be described.
Introduces Sonnet 5; provider evaluations are evidence of reported capability under the stated test conditions.
Launches an AI workbench for scientists; tools and access do not replace experimental verification.
Introduces a partner network for deployment support; a program launch does not measure partner delivery quality or customer outcomes.
Announces TCS's planned Claude rollout in regulated industries; training and deployment targets are forward-looking commitments.

Announces DXC integration into regulated-industry systems; promised access requires application-specific controls and rollout verification.
Introduces Fable and Mythos before later restrictions and redeployment; use the later September update for current positioning.
Plans broader Glasswing access subject to security conditions; a target organization count does not equal completed onboarding.
Reports groundbreaking for Michigan infrastructure; beginning construction is different from operating installed capacity.
Confirms submission of a confidential draft registration statement; this does not establish a completed IPO or public listing.
Introduces Opus 4.8; newer releases in this catalog supersede its position as a frontier announcement.
Announces a Series H round and post-money valuation; a financing-round valuation is distinct from liquid market capitalization or profitability.
Announces a KPMG alliance with broad workforce access; eligible employees are not a count of active users or proven productivity gains.
Announces Codex deployment in hybrid and on-premises environments; deployment locality does not imply downloadable model weights.
Announces Anthropic's acquisition of Stainless; developer tooling can support distribution, but acquisition alone does not prove integration benefits.
Describes PwC deployment across client and internal functions; partner claims do not establish representative commercial results.
Links additional compute to higher Claude usage limits; contracted resources and resulting product quotas are different measurements.
Introduces financial-workflow agents and templates; suitability, access controls and review depend on each firm's task.
Creates an enterprise AI-services venture with financial sponsors; it signals implementation investment without proving the venture's returns.
Reports secured compute capacity commitments; secured or contracted capacity should not be labeled fully online capacity.
Updates Microsoft's and OpenAI's partnership terms; the announcement describes the agreement at that date.
Attributes Claude Code quality regressions to specific changes and describes fixes; a model label alone does not capture harness behavior.
Announces an Amazon compute expansion up to a future capacity target; delivery timing and contractual conditions matter.
Separates managed-agent orchestration, execution and persistent state; that architecture supports operation but does not guarantee task correctness.
Plans future TPU capacity with Google and Broadcom; expected later availability is not current deployed compute.
Describes a permission classifier for coding agents; frequent user approval is not evidence that every requested action is safe.
Explores harness design for long-running development; completion claims still require externally checkable outcomes.
Commits funding to a partner network; a spending commitment is neither equity financing nor measured revenue.
Reports benchmark awareness and possible contamination in selected runs; the observed sample cannot establish a general real-world rate.
Announces Amazon's strategic investment and commercial partnership; later financial filings provide stronger evidence of executed payments.
Updates Anthropic's scaling policy; a voluntary organizational framework is distinct from legal oversight or guaranteed compliance.
Announces consulting alliances for enterprise adoption; partnerships are distribution evidence, not independently verified client outcomes.
Announces Series G funding and a post-money valuation; the later Series H is a separate round, and valuations must not be added together.
Measures infrastructure-induced variation in coding-agent evaluations; controlled environments matter when comparing small score changes.
Reports an agent-built compiler experiment; its scope and remaining limitations prevent a general claim of autonomous software engineering.
Announces a multiyear commercial agreement with Snowflake; the contract value is not an equity investment in OpenAI.
Describes adapting hiring evaluations as models improve; an assessment's resistance to assistance can change over time.
Adds Cerebras to inference infrastructure; a partnership supports capacity strategy without establishing universal latency gains.
Combines investment and energy-infrastructure partnership announcements; distinct financing instruments should not be conflated or double-counted.
Explains agent evaluation principles, trajectories and graders; useful guidance still needs a task-specific, human-authored success definition.
Announces investment and a compute-linked facility for Anthropic; S110 subsequently specifies exercised amounts and the remaining facility.
